# ADR 0012: Review Tool Shapes Are Generated by Orval and Hidden by the Module

## Date

2026-11-27

## Context

Our rules already ask for a [[Contract]] behind every shape and for opaque [[Domain object]]s. They do not say by
which means the review tool satisfies them, and an [[AI agent]] left to itself picks other means each time.

## Decisions

1. **[OpenAPI](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/latest.html) describes each [[Interface]] and [Orval](https://orval.dev/)
   generates from it.** This covers the domain model and each [[Interface]] of a client, a controller and an adapter.

2. **Generation is one step of the build.** The build invokes Orval, and the configuration of Orval points to each
   [[Contract]]. No generator of our own and no second step stands beside it.

3. **The folders of the [[Generated code]] mirror the folders of the [[Layer]]s.** Each [[Layer]] has one subfolder.

4. **An [[AI agent]] sees only what it needs.** The main agent and the sub agent each have a client of their own, and
   the sub agent only reports.

5. **The [[Contract]] of a client holds its answers and its help.** The answers are described in that [[Contract]], not
   beside it. Help prints the descriptions that the [[Contract]] already holds, and nothing else.

6. **A [[Domain object]] is one value: its exposed shape with the methods of its [[Interface]] added.** Orval writes
   the exposed shape, with [Zod](https://zod.dev/) at its defaults. The domain names the value only by its
   [[Interface]] and never reads the exposed shape.

7. **The [[Module]] hides the exposed shape.** Code inside the [[Module]] of a [[Domain object]] reads its exposed
   shape; code in any other [[Module]] cannot. No brand, symbol or tag marks a [[Domain object]].

8. **A [[Domain object]] is a [[Class]] where that reads better.**

9. **A [[Domain method]] on two [[Domain object]]s is on the one where the call reads better.** The [[Change]] answers
   the outcome for a complete [[Ledger]].

10. **A [Zod codec](https://zod.dev/codecs) is the only transformation.** Each of its two sides comes from a
    [[Contract]]. An adapter turns a host response into a [[Domain object]] with a Zod codec, and the command line turns
    its arguments into [[Domain object]]s the same way.

11. **A value goes in with decode and out with encode.** No function is named unwrap.

12. **The one perimeters folder holds the parsing and the Zod codecs.** No other folder holds them.

13. **A host adapter takes a URL and answers the [[Change]].** The URL is opaque in the domain.

14. **A delegating adapter asks each implementing adapter in turn.** An implementing adapter answers one of three
    things: that it does not know the format, a failure the domain defines, or the [[Change]].

15. **An implementing adapter calls its host through a generated client that holds only the operations it needs.** It
    reads a token from the environment when the environment holds one.

16. **Everything that is specific to git is in the git adapter.**

17. **The [[Change]] holds its [[Checkout]].** A client that does not need the [[Checkout]] never receives it.

18. **A probe is dispatched from the stored review.** A persistence adapter stores the review, in memory or on disk.

19. **A probe is data.** It is an entry in YAML, as a rule is, and not a type. It names the one group whose rules it
    judges.

20. **A probe holds no permission beyond its need.** A normal probe has no [[Access to filesystem]].

21. **The controllers and their [[Unit test]]s are finished first.** A [[Unit test]] of a controller replaces every
    adapter with a stand-in, and both stay unchanged while the domain and the adapters are built.

22. **Production code, the mock hosts and the [[Integration test]]s share nothing but HTTP.** Each of the three has a
    folder of its own, and none imports from another.

23. **One [[Immutable]] git repository is the single source of every use case.** Each use case is a branch, and no
    [[Test]] changes the repository. The git adapter reads it as it is, over HTTP.

24. **All three hosts hold the same use cases.** Orval writes the mock hosts for GitHub and Azure DevOps. A mock host
    takes its state from that repository and keeps none of its own.

25. **The repository stores each earlier review in `.reviews` as JSON, as it was reported.** For the mock hosts a stored
    review is only a fixture; for plain git it can be a real one.

26. **A mock host keeps a log to assert on.** Production code keeps none.

27. **Building the mock hosts and serving them are two build targets.** The build ends before the serving starts.

28. **[[Unit test]]s reach 90% [[Code coverage]], of lines and of branches.**
